name: Strategy Game Wrapper
summary: Correct answers earn in-game currency/resources that players invest strategically (towers, upgrades, inventory, crops) to progress through a game world.

aiGenerability.notes: AI generates questions excellently. Game shells are pre-built; AI fills them with thematic questions. Game design (upgrade trees, economies) must be hand-authored but are reusable templates.

currencyPerQuestion.description: Base amount of currency earned per correct question (e.g., 10).

questionMechanic.description: ID of the wrapped question mechanic (e.g., 'multiple-choice', 'short-answer').

questions.description: Array of question objects conforming to the wrapped mechanic's schema.

upgradeTree.description: Pre-defined upgrade/resource options players can purchase (towers, crops, decorations, etc.). Each has: id, name, cost (currency), effect (descriptive), icon.

questionsPerRound.description: Number of questions before player can make strategic purchases/upgrades (typical 2-5).

roundCount.description: Total number of rounds in a session (typical 5-10 for 5-10 min gameplay).

winCondition.description: What constitutes a win (e.g., 'accumulate 500 gold', 'defend 10 waves', 'fill all farm plots').

ux.mobileNotes: Split-screen: game world (top 60%) with interactive upgrade targets. Question pop-up overlay (bottom 40%). Currency/score HUD sticky at top. Tap to answer question, tap to purchase/place upgrade. Large upgrade icons with tap/hold to preview.

ageAdaptations.8-10: Simple 1-resource economy (just gold). 3-5 easy upgrades (walls, trees). 2-3 question rounds per purchase opportunity. Abundant currency to encourage exploration.
ageAdaptations.11-13: Multi-resource economy (gold + special resources). 5-10 upgrades with cost tiers. 3-5 question rounds per opportunity. Optional synergies (e.g., towers boost each other).
ageAdaptations.14-16: Complex economy with resource conversion. 15+ upgrades with dependencies. 5-10 question rounds; optional time gates. Advanced: leaderboard, prestige mechanics, asymmetric strategies.
